history.alt_text: Glass prism splitting one beam of light into sixteen parallel copper rays across a steel bench in a dark server room
history.caption: One beam in, sixteen metered rays out — the fan-out finds its price tag.
history.title: Beam-splitter fan-out: sixteen rays, one bill

style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio photograph in a dark server room, split-screen diptych divided by a heavy optical beam-splitter prism standing on a brushed-steel bench plate. Left third: near-black graphite quiet, a single copper-warm beam entering low from the left through thin air. On the seam the prism splits it into sixteen razor-thin parallel copper rays raking right across brushed steel toward a row of dim server racks, each ray landing in a small hard contact glow like a metered line item. Three-quarter angle, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, graphite, charcoal and copper palette with steel-blue rack glow behind, visible long contact shadow, fine film grain, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: This is a pricing story — an effort level literally went on sale — so a product treatment of the mechanism-as-object fits, and the vertical's sanctioned metaphor for agent fan-out is photonic: one beam split into parallel rays. Studio staging on real brushed steel in a dark server room keeps physical weight and contact shadows instead of a floating render.
subject: a beam-splitter prism dividing one beam of light into sixteen parallel rays — the agent fan-out made physical
core_thesis: A vendor now sells a 16-agent fan-out as a quality tier the same week an equal-cost study priced that parallel pattern at 2.6–3.8× one agent's spend for only 1–5 hidden-test points — headcount is a price dial, not a quality dial.
core_conflict: Fan-out headcount sold as quality (up to 16 workers, one lead) versus the measured return (a lone, better-instructed agent matching it at a fraction of the cost)
composition: split-screen diptych: dark quiet single-beam left third, prism on the seam, sixteen-ray fan-out blazing right, extreme asymmetry with wide negative space

review.depicts: A single orange light beam enters from the left across a dark reflective studio surface, strikes a vertical transparent glass panel standing on the seam, and splits into a fan of parallel orange rays that converge onto a row of small glowing points on the right, with dark server racks with blue indicator lights in the background.
review.reason: The image physically renders the article's own mechanism — one input beam split into many parallel rays, i.e., the agent fan-out — in a server-room setting, with no text, competing industry, or contradictory scene.

input.prompt:
Studio photograph in a dark server room, split-screen diptych divided by a heavy optical beam-splitter prism standing on a brushed-steel bench plate. Left third: near-black graphite quiet, a single copper-warm beam entering low from the left through thin air. On the seam the prism splits it into sixteen razor-thin parallel copper rays raking right across brushed steel toward a row of dim server racks, each ray landing in a small hard contact glow like a metered line item. Three-quarter angle, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, graphite, charcoal and copper palette with steel-blue rack glow behind, visible long contact shadow, fine film grain, no people.

Do not include: people, faces, hands, garbled text, random lettering, numbers, signage, watermarks, UI, logos.
